A_target.statement:
Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a [[Definition:Graph (Graph Theory)|graph]] and $k \in \Z_{>0}$.
Then there exists a [[Definition:Conjunctive Normal Form|CNF]] [[Definition:Boolean Formula|formula]] $\phi_{G, k}$, computable in polynomial time, such that:
:$G$ is [[Definition:K-Colorable Graph|$k$-colorable]] $\iff \phi_{G, k}$ is [[Definition:Satisfiable|satisfiable]]

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Boolean Satisfiability Problem|satisfiability problem]] asks, for a [[Definition:Boolean Formula|Boolean formula]] $\phi$, whether there exists a [[Definition:Boolean Interpretation|truth assignment]] $v$ with $\map v \phi = \T$.

substitutions.the k colors: for each vertex, a clause forcing at least one color
substitutions.edge (u,v): clauses forbidding u and v sharing a color

derived.adjacent vertices differ: no clause (x_{u,c} and x_{v,c}) both true

validity_conditions: The formula phi encodes exactly: each vertex gets at least one color, and no edge is monochromatic; its satisfying assignments correspond bijectively to proper k-colorings.
phi is constructible in polynomial time in the size of G, so the reduction is valid.
proof_plan: Introduce a Boolean variable $x_{v, c}$ for each $v \in V$ and color $c \in \set {1, \ldots, k}$.

Add the clauses:
:$\displaystyle \bigvee_{c \mathop = 1}^k x_{v, c}$ for each $v \in V$
:$\neg x_{u, c} \lor \neg x_{v, c}$ for each $u v \in E$ and each $c$

A satisfying assignment gives each vertex at least one color with no edge monochromatic; choosing one such color per vertex is a [[Definition:Proper Vertex Coloring|proper $k$-coloring]].
Conversely, a proper $k$-coloring gives a satisfying assignment.
